items.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I saw her do it in the three years that I worked for her.

ctx.x: So you returned to San Diego. Was that always your home base after Vegas? Or did you move around some?

Let’s see. No I went back to Las Vegas at that point, had a little jazz gig in town, like an after-hours thing, it started at one or two in the morning and went until five or something. And I was playing the “Viva Le Girls” show before that. So I was playing my regular, it was in the lounge at the old Dunes Hotel, and then I’d run down and play this jazz gig all night. And Gus Mancuso, who is a wonderful musician who has lived in Vegas for many years, plays all kinds of instruments, one of those guys, recommended…

items.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Bob has recorded and performed with a long list of major artists including Sarah Vaughn

ctx.x: Bob Magnusson was born in New York City on February 24, 1947 and grew up in San Diego surrounded by music. He first played French horn and took up the bass in 1967, joining the Buddy Rich band a year later. Bob has recorded and performed with a long list of major artists including Sarah Vaughn, Art Pepper, Linda Ronstadt and Roger Kellaway. He lives in San Diego where he often performs with flautist Holly Hofmann and pianist Mike Wofford.
Bob was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 14, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
